rule: mixed: the repelling relation and the nightmoth genus come through, but because the coined term sits in sentence-initial position the translator cannot tell a capitalised name from an ordinary lowercase substance word, so it emits (Name wintergloss "Wintergloss") and makes wintergloss a named individual here while every other sentence in this item treats it as a substance; it also files the standing generic as one dispositional event instead of the kind-to-kind relation that two bare kind nouns license. Rewrite so the term is not sentence-initial, e.g. "Nightmoths are repelled by wintergloss."
texts: bad: the rule can never fire — the trigger clause's burning is written as a constructed term (sk_burn $x) inside the condition, and a condition can only match atoms that already exist in the knowledge base, so no actual burning ever sets it off; the culprit is the indefinite "a lantern" that the second clause then has to point back at as "that lantern". Rewrite with the lantern as the subject of the condition clause and an explicit occurrence quantifier: "Whenever a lantern burns wintergloss, the wintergloss repels nightmoths from that lantern."

bad: "that lantern" points at nothing — the condition clause never mentions a lantern — so the parse silently invents one and adds a burning-in-a-lantern condition the sentence does not state. Rewrite to introduce the lantern in the condition clause itself, and make it that clause's subject so it binds cleanly: "If a lantern burns wintergloss alongside mire-essence, nightmoths avoid that lantern."

good. "rarely" lands as a strength-0.1 rule that hands the habit to each member of the Keepers, the surface word is kept in a companion atom, and burning wintergloss takes the consumed-object role with no tense on the habitual.

mixed: the Stilllight Lantern and the "sometimes" strength are handled well, but "the Keepers" becomes a bare name here — one unclassified individual — while the previous sentence made it a group of keepers, so the two sentences' facts never meet on one symbol; the positive habit is also packed into a single strength-0.5 bundle, the shape otherwise reserved for denials, so its role atoms are not separately queryable. Write the group the same way in both sentences, e.g. "The keepers sometimes burn wintergloss at the Stilllight Lantern.", which yields the same distributing rule the previous sentence got.
